profiles.description: Hands-on technical engineer who builds and validates the carrier's IT disaster recovery capability. Per the packet responsibilities, the role defines recovery objectives (RTO/RPO) for critical systems, maintains DR runbooks and replication configurations, executes DR and failover tests, and validates recovery results while remediating identified gaps. Industry sources describe this as an infrastructure/systems engineering specialization covering backup and replication architecture, runbook automation, and regular failover exercises from tabletop drills to full recovery simulations. At this carrier the role executes the technical recovery work that the Disaster Recovery Manager governs.

proposedOrgUnit.rationale: DR engineering is infrastructure-layer work (replication, standby environments, backup/failover) that sits naturally with the infrastructure teams, distinct from the DR Manager who governs the program from Operations' Vendor & Resilience department.

profiles.notes: Packet has no value streams, tasks, or deliverables (counts all zero) — profile grounded in packet responsibilities plus research. Prior roleFamily was 'Specialist'; research (Nadcab, MHA) frames this as a systems/infrastructure engineering role, so 'Engineering' is used and the prior disagreement recorded here.

profiles.description: Owns the carrier's technology recovery program from the Operations division's Vendor & Resilience department, leading the Risk Compliance Audit and Cybersecurity, Identity & Resilience value streams. Per the packet, the role owns DR strategy and recovery objectives: mapping critical applications to infrastructure recovery requirements, defining recovery strategy options per critical application, authoring and drift-reconciling recovery runbooks, provisioning standby DR infrastructure and replication links, and validating backup coverage and job completion for critical data. It also coordinates service restoration sequencing during recovery events and participates in assessing the DR plan against regulatory resilience expectations. Industry postings for BC/DR managers at financial-services firms confirm this mix of program governance, annual test design, and coordination with infrastructure, security, and business continuity stakeholders.

profiles.description: Manages the operational backbone of the carrier's distribution channels from the Sales, Distribution & Marketing division, leading the Sales Distribution Marketing and Call Center value streams. Per the packet, the role owns the distribution operating-model design — documenting end-to-end roles across channels, defining producer servicing processes and support tiers, configuring distribution workflows in the portal and CRM, and setting KPIs and governance cadence. It also owns producer/broker service support (authenticating producers, resolving commission and statement questions, escalations), adjudicates sales compensation disputes, and handles producer complaint and suitability escalations including remediation or disciplinary referral. Carrier job postings for distribution/commissions operations leadership confirm this combination of producer onboarding workflow ownership, commission accuracy stewardship, hierarchy management, and dispute/appeal handling.

profiles.description: Executes the day-to-day producer lifecycle administration that keeps the carrier's distribution channels ready to sell. Per the packet, the role owns producer contracting and appointment work — collecting executed agreements and required documentation, creating producer master records and assigning producer codes, and recording agreement terms in the contract repository — plus running new-producer activation readiness checklists, maintaining producer hierarchy and book-of-business records in the CRM, reconciling agency-to-producer relationships for master data quality, and publishing product and rate collateral to the producer portal. It participates in sales compensation administration (configuring incentive rules, validating attainment data, calculating payouts). AgentSync's producer-management literature confirms this contracting/appointment/onboarding scope as the core carrier-side producer operations role.

profiles.description: Leads employee relations casework and the HR policy machinery for the carrier from the Human Resources & Talent division. Per the packet, the role owns HR policy development and governance (scoping policy gaps against regulatory triggers, drafting policy with employment law counsel), performance improvement planning (assessing PIP eligibility and determining outcomes), and employee separations (validating separation reasons and approvals, initiating offboarding, conducting exit interviews). It also owns registering employee professional licenses and certifications and obtaining breach-response sign-off from the Data Protection Officer in privacy incidents. Industry job descriptions confirm ER managers conduct workplace investigations, oversee disciplinary actions and consistent policy application, and handle grievances and separations with discretion — matching the packet's case management, investigations, and progressive discipline deliverables.

Privacy breach sign-off tasks are plausible for HR-data incidents.

profiles.description: Processes mid-term policy changes across the carrier's book from Policy Operations, supporting the Business Operations value stream. Per the packet, the role participates in the endorsement lifecycle — intaking requests and confirming authorized requestors, rating endorsements and calculating pro-rata premium adjustments, issuing endorsements and updating the in-force policy record — plus adjacent transactions: return-premium calculation on cancellations, mid-term billing changes, premium refunds, and retirement-services items such as auto-enrollment defaults and 1099-R withholding coding. NAIC guidance confirms endorsements add, delete, exclude, or change coverage mid-term with corresponding premium adjustment, and industry sources describe the pro-rata calculation the role applies so premium matches the coverage actually in force.

profiles.description: Defines and governs the carrier's target technology landscape from the Technology & Engineering division's executive leadership, leading the Technology Strategy, Architecture & Delivery, Technology Engineering, and Product Delivery value streams. Per the packet, the role owns technology strategy and roadmap planning (assessing current-state capability and gaps), convenes the Architecture Review Board to adjudicate design submissions, records architecture decisions and dispensations in the decision register, and maps end-to-end resources supporting each important business service. It also participates in enterprise target-state definition and capability gap analysis, and its responsibilities cover standards and platform guardrails, application portfolio rationalization, technical debt planning, and build-versus-buy advice. Industry sources confirm EAs chair architecture review boards, maintain decision logs and standards catalogs, and own multi-year roadmaps connecting business strategy to platform evolution.

profiles.description: Runs the carrier's enterprise risk management framework from the Risk, Compliance & Audit division, leading the Risk Compliance Audit, Corporate Functions Operations, and Legal Corporate Governance value streams. Per the packet, the role owns the risk universe and taxonomy (cataloging enterprise risk categories hierarchically and publishing the approved taxonomy), the risk appetite framework (drafting quantitative appetite statements by category and setting tolerance thresholds and escalation triggers per limit), and regulatory change compliance operations (translating regulatory requirements into control changes, testing post-change compliance, and attesting implementation). It also assembles the Form F enterprise risk report for the insurance group and supports operational resilience deliverables including stress testing and scenario analysis. NAIC and industry ORSA guidance confirm exactly this scope — risk identification and taxonomy, formal risk appetite statements with tolerances and limits, stress-tested assessments, and holding-company risk reporting via Form F.

profiles.description: Builds and maintains the data pipelines that feed the carrier's warehouse and analytics platforms from the Data & AI division's Data Engineering department, leading in the Data AI value stream. Per the packet, the role owns developing cleansing and standardization transforms, executing source-to-target reconciliation as a pipeline quality gate, and ingesting and versioning external reference data such as ISO, NAIC, and postal updates. It participates across the data management stack: harvesting metadata and constructing column-level lineage, profiling datasets and deploying automated quality checks, applying masking and tokenization to sensitive fields, and automating archival of aged data. Industry sources confirm ETL developers act as gatekeepers of data quality and consistency — designing transformations, implementing validation and reconciliation controls, tuning job performance, and documenting mappings for production support.

profiles.description: Provides high-trust administrative support to the CEO and executive leadership team from the Office of the CEO. Per the packet responsibilities, the role manages C-suite calendars against board, regulator, and earnings commitments; arranges travel and expenses; screens and routes correspondence with immediate flagging of regulatory, legal, and media-sensitive items; prepares and distributes executive agendas and minutes; maintains delegation-of-authority records and signature routing; and coordinates onsite logistics for board meetings, rating-agency visits, and regulator examinations. Its graph tasks are all Participant roles in corporate resilience processes — supporting crisis-team activation, stakeholder crisis communications, and resilience evidence compilation and filing — reflecting the coordination and logistics support the office provides during major disruptions. Industry sources confirm the EA-to-CEO role centers on calendar mastery, board material preparation, confidentiality, and liaising with boards and senior management on the CEO's behalf.

profiles.description: Owns executive and crisis messaging for the carrier from the Office of the CEO, leading in the Corporate Functions Operations and Risk Compliance Audit value streams. Per the packet, the role owns coordinating stakeholder and customer crisis communications and preparing pre-approved holding statements and message templates, and participates in defining crisis-management roles, escalation thresholds, and decision authority and in preparing the operations performance pack for leadership review. Its responsibilities cover drafting CEO speeches, town-hall scripts, and earnings-call talking points; coordinating Legal and Compliance review of external CEO statements; planning the internal communications calendar; and measuring message reach and employee sentiment. Industry job descriptions confirm executive communications managers create speeches and executive content, run internal communication plans, and lead crisis communications planning and rapid coordinated response.

profiles.description: Manages the carrier's catastrophe and accumulation risk controls from the Underwriting division's Specialty Support department, leading in the Underwriting value stream. Per the packet, the role owns comparing zonal accumulation against approved capacity limits and participates in aggregating total insured value by catastrophe zone; its responsibilities extend to maintaining exposure triggers, tolerance thresholds, and escalation routines, reviewing model outputs and concentration breaches, and coordinating exposure views with underwriting, actuarial, CAT modeling, and reinsurance teams. Industry sources confirm exposure management teams enforce internal aggregation limits per high-risk segment, monitor TIV concentration by geographic zone, and supply portfolio exposure insight that underpins underwriting capacity and reinsurance decisions.

profiles.description: Underwrites and places individual-risk reinsurance for the carrier from the Reinsurance division's Facultative Placement department, leading the Reinsurance and Underwriting value streams. Per the packet, the role works both directions of facultative business: on the ceded side it determines facultative need beyond treaty capacity, calculates net line retention after planned cessions, confirms reinsurance terms before the underlying risk is bound, and prepares facultative submissions for reinsurer review; on the assumed side it triages inbound submissions against appetite, documents underwriting rationale, issues firm order quotes to brokers, and drafts and verifies slips, clauses, exclusions, and territorial scope. Industry sources confirm facultative reinsurance is negotiated risk-by-risk for exposures exceeding treaty capacity, with the underwriter performing exhaustive individual risk assessment, bespoke pricing, and certificate/slip documentation.

profiles.description: Investigates property and casualty losses on site for the Claims division, leading in the Claims value stream. Per the packet, the role owns capturing field inspection findings and damage estimates on site, capturing site photos and physical evidence, conducting and recording party and witness statements, coordinating site access and inspection logistics, and documenting pre-loss condition during emergency mitigation — plus CAT field operations work during catastrophe events. It participates in initial severity assessment and reserving, investigation planning, and damage valuation. This maps directly to the O*NET Claims Adjusters, Examiners, and Investigators occupation (13-1031.00), which lists Field Claims Adjuster as a sample title and describes investigating and assessing property damage, interviewing claimants and witnesses, and creating damage estimates; industry accounts of field adjusting confirm the inspection, photo documentation, reporting, and catastrophe deployment rhythm.

profiles.description: Performs FP&A work for the carrier from Finance & Investments' Planning & Capital department, leading in the Finance Investments value stream and supporting Actuarial, Underwriting, HR, PMO, and Technology streams. Per the packet, the role owns running multi-scenario sensitivity analysis on the long-range plan and refreshing rolling-forecast drivers with latest actuals and pipeline data, and participates broadly as the finance partner across the enterprise: cost-of-capital charges for internal transfer pricing, business cases for project funding decisions, cloud budget-to-actual variance analysis and spend forecasts, incentive accrual reconciliation, and project cost control. Industry FP&A sources confirm this profile — building budgets and rolling forecasts, performing variance analysis with driver commentary, running scenario/what-if analysis, and business partnering with operating departments — and place the analyst title at the individual-contributor tier of the FP&A ladder.
